#6

However, every Z2\mathbb{Z}_2Z2​-graded-commutative ring can be naturally regarded as a τ≤1S\tau_{\leq1}\mathbb{S}τ≤1​S-graded ring by putting everything into degree 000 and 111 and by choosing the σk\sigma_kσk​ automorphisms to be given by a↦−aa\mapsto-aa↦−a.

Absolutey, it’s the formalization of this phenomenon, via that Proposition, which yields the definition proposed at spectral super-scheme!

I am not saying this cannot be integrated into the perspective you adopted, just saying that it would need to be integrated to be a satisfactory reply to “What is higher superalgebra?” (The same remark applies to Kapronov’s proposal! and in fact it applies to a sizeable community of “NQ-manifold” theorists out there.) In fact, it seems pretty clear for how to integrate this into you scheme: You can enhance it to speak of higher graded algebras over higher graded base rings, and then you just have to require the higher graded base ring to be 2-periodic. I think.

What I found fascinating about the proposal at spectral super-scheme is that the identification of super-grading with foundations of algebraic topology ranges even deeper than in Kapranov’s proposal: It’s really the notion of E∞E_\inftyE∞​-algebra as such that already captures “higher Z\mathbb{Z}Z-graded super-algebra” and then the choice of even periodic base ring spectra (which are known to play a pivotal role in chromatic theory etc.) makes it genuinely super-algebraic in the sense of physics.

#23

Why are general E∞E_\inftyE∞​-monoids canonically (and non-trivially) S\mathbb{S}S-graded, though?

I assume that by asking “Why?” you do not mean “How does Sagave-Schlichtkrull’s proof work?”, but you do mean to ask for a conceptual explanation.

I would turn this around: The observation that they are is a peek into the fundamental nature of reality, and is a hint for a deep relation between higher- and super- geometry/algebra, a hint that remains to be fully followed up on.

At the coarse level of homotopy groups, this is an old observation in algebraic topology, embodied in classical phenomena such as the super Lie algebra structure of Whitehead products.

My gut feeling here is that ultimately algebraic topology/homotopy theory is part of the explanation of “Why super-mathematics?” Namely: Super-algebra (in an enhanced form) seems to be the algebra/geometry automatically appearing in homotopy-theoretic foundations.

but does it also give a way to go from I\mathcal{I}I-spaces to J\mathcal{J}J-spaces?

Good question, I am wondering about this each time I pick up their article. I don’t know. (Maybe this is explained somewhere in their writing, but I haven’t spent more time with it, I have to admit.)

The picture I have is:

While each E∞E_\inftyE∞​-spectrum carries a canonical S\mathbb{S}S-grading in that it maps to an E∞E_\inftyE∞​-monoid in J\mathcal{J}J-spaces (via their right adjoint functor ΩJ\Omega^{\mathcal{J}}ΩJ in their equation (4.4)), the plain morphisms of E∞E_\inftyE∞​-monoids need not respect this S\mathbb{S}S-grading. Instead, the E∞E_\inftyE∞​-morphisms that respect the canonical S\mathbb{S}S-grading are those in the category of E∞E_\inftyE∞​-monoids in J\mathcal{J}J-spaces.

#25 The result of Sagave-Schlichtkrull seems slightly misleading to me. A more natural statement would be a grading by the Picard ∞\infty∞-groupoid of invertible spectra. For any presentably symmetric monoidal ∞\infty∞-category CCC, there is by the universal property of Day convolution a symmetric monoidal adjunction between Fun(Pic(C),Spc)\mathrm{Fun}(\mathrm{Pic}(C),\mathrm{Spc})Fun(Pic(C),Spc) and CCC. The right adjoint sends an (E∞E_\inftyE∞​-)object ccc to a $\Pic(C)$-graded (E∞E_\inftyE∞​-)space, whose unit component is Map(1,c)\mathrm{Map}(1,c)Map(1,c). Now given a particular invertible object L∈Pic(C)L\in {\mathrm{Pic}}(C)L∈Pic(C), there is a unique E∞E_\inftyE∞​-map Ω∞S→Pic(C)\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}\to {\mathrm{Pic}}(C)Ω∞S→Pic(C) sending 111 to LLL by the universal property of Ω∞S\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}Ω∞S, so any Pic(C)\mathrm{Pic}(C)Pic(C)-graded space gives rise to an Ω∞S\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}Ω∞S-graded space.

If I understand correctly, the Sagave-Schlichtkrull Ω∞S\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}Ω∞S-graded space is obtained via this construction applied to L=ΣSL=\Sigma\mathbb{S}L=ΣS. But going from the Pic(Sp)\mathrm{Pic}(\mathrm{Sp})Pic(Sp)-grading to the Ω∞S\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}Ω∞S-grading seems to forget a lot of information. For example at the level of homotopy groups the E∞E_\inftyE∞​-map Ω∞S→Pic(Sp)\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}\to {\mathrm{Pic}}(\mathrm{Sp})Ω∞S→Pic(Sp) is a map πnS→πn−1S\pi_n\mathbb{S}\to \pi_{n-1}\mathbb{S}πn​S→πn−1​S (for n≥2n\geq 2n≥2).

On the other hand the map Ω∞S→Pic(Sp)\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}\to {\mathrm{Pic}}(\mathrm{Sp})Ω∞S→Pic(Sp) is an equivalence on 111-truncations, so for graded objects in 1-categories there is no difference.

Sagave–Schlichtkrull prove that any symmetric spectrum EEE has an underlying S\mathbb{S}S-graded E∞\mathbb{E}_\inftyE∞​-space ΩJ(E)\Omega^\mathcal{J}(E)ΩJ(E)

Could you please elaborate on this a bit? I’m unsure about how to construct this adjunction (which universal property of Day convolution are you using?)

The universal property is HA 4.8.1.10 (4) (in the special case of Cor. 4.8.1.12): If AAA is symmetric monoidal, the Day convolution on PSh(A)\mathrm{PSh}(A)PSh(A) is the universal cocomplete symmetric monoidal category under A where the tensor product preserves colimits in each variable.

Also, (if I understand it correcty) the construction you describe builds ΩJ(E)\Omega^\mathcal{J}(E)ΩJ(E) as a lax symmetric monoidal functor Ω∞S→Spc\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}\to {\mathrm{Spc}}Ω∞S→Spc, though Sagave–Schlichtkrull seem to view an Ω∞S\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}Ω∞S-grading as instead a morphism of E∞\mathbb{E}_\inftyE∞​-spaces ΩJ(E)→Ω∞S\Omega^\mathcal{J}(E)\to\Omega^\infty\mathbb{S}ΩJ(E)→Ω∞S, “going in the opposite direction”. Do you know how these two definitions compare with each other?

They are equivalent by a symmetric monoidal version of straightening/unstraightening. Namely, if KKK is an E∞E_\inftyE∞​-space, the equivalence Spc/K=Fun(K,Spc)\mathrm{Spc}/K = \mathrm{Fun}(K,\mathrm{Spc})Spc/K=Fun(K,Spc) is symmetric monoidal. I don’t know a direct reference for this but I guess it can be deduced from HA 4.8.1.12 which characterizes the RHS.
